text:
- **chief complaint:** Follow-up for chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction, and pre-operative evaluation before planned right knee replacement.
- **history of present illness:** Heart failure exacerbation in spring with rising BMP (3,000 in March, 6,000 in April) and increasing dyspnea. Furosemide was switched to torsemide. Lisinopril was increased in March. Now weight is down about 3 to 3.5 pounds and symptoms have improved. Heartburn resolved after a course of Prilosec.
- **physical examination:** Lungs sound good; breathing is non-labored.
- **symptoms experienced by the patient:** Leg cramps (relieved with pickle juice), urinary urgency (much improved on oxybutynin), prior dyspnea (improved), heartburn (resolved).
- **new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages:** Torsemide 20 mg by mouth daily (replaced furosemide). Lisinopril 10 mg daily (increased in March). Magnesium supplement recommended, dosage not specified, twice daily.
- **follow-up instructions:** Repeat EKG today. Hold clopidogrel for one week before surgery. Pre-op check in the first or second week of June. Right knee replacement at end of June. Screening colonoscopy within the next 30 days. Repeat A1c may be needed before surgery. Pending heart failure lab results.
